passage:
Counselling note, Thursday. Lalremsiami came in after the police traced the car through a camera near the bus stand. The story came in short bursts: a pedestrian had stepped out at dusk, the bumper caught the person's leg, a crowd shouted and closed in, Lalremsiami's mind went white and the car drove off without stopping. The pedestrian sat by the road until a passer-by phoned for an ambulance. "If I'd stayed, it would have been a small thing," Lalremsiami kept saying. Now there is an added complaint for leaving, the pedestrian's family is angry, and Lalremsiami has stopped sleeping. I listened and did not argue, but said that being afraid is not the same as the matter being over. I can't advise on legal questions, so I gave the details of the legal aid clinic and offered to sit with Lalremsiami when facing the family.

Preeti, counsellor

qa.q: How did the police trace the car?
qa.a: The police traced the car through a camera near the bus stand.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling when the crowd closed in?
qa.a: Lalremsiami was frightened and panicked, and the mind went white.

qa.q: What could Lalremsiami have done instead of driving off, and why?
qa.a: Lalremsiami could have stayed, called for an ambulance and the police, and let them manage the angry crowd, because staying gets help to the injured person and stops the trouble from growing.

qa.q: How might the pedestrian have felt sitting by the road?
qa.a: The pedestrian was probably hurt and abandoned, waiting until a passer-by phoned for an ambulance.

grounding: Illustrates a driver panicking at a crowd and fleeing after hitting a pedestrian, leaving the injured person without help and adding trouble.

passage:
Wednesday, midnight.
I don't know how to write this. At about eight, on the lane behind the market, a man stepped out and my car hit him. He fell. People started running towards the car, shouting. I was so scared of the crowd that I pressed the accelerator and drove away.
I drove around for an hour. My hands wouldn't stop. I kept seeing him on the ground.
At ten I called Jeevan and told him everything. He said, "You have to go back and tell the police. Now. Tell your father." I told Papa. He didn't shout. He just picked up the car keys and we went to the police station together.
At the station they said a shopkeeper had taken the man to hospital nearly twenty minutes after I left. He has a broken leg. The officer said leaving had made everything much worse, for him and for me.
I left a man lying in the road because I was afraid.
Shankar

qa.q: Who took the injured man to hospital?
qa.a: A shopkeeper took him to hospital, nearly twenty minutes after Shankar left.

qa.q: Why did Shankar drive away, and how does Shankar feel now?
qa.a: Shankar was terrified of the crowd, and now feels guilty and ashamed about leaving a hurt man lying in the road.

qa.q: What should Shankar have done instead of driving away?
qa.a: Shankar should have stopped, called 112 and stayed or waited somewhere safe nearby for the police, because the injured man needed help first.

qa.q: How was the injured man affected by Shankar's choice?
qa.a: He lay injured for nearly twenty minutes before a shopkeeper took him to hospital, time in which he got no help.

grounding: Shows a panicked driver fleeing after hitting a pedestrian, which delays help and worsens the trouble, before going to the police with a parent.

Pradeep: where are you? your mum called me
Nilesh: I hit someone with the bike near the bus stand
Pradeep: WHAT. is he ok??
Nilesh: I don't know. people were running at me. I got scared and rode off
Pradeep: Nilesh you have to go back
Nilesh: they'll beat me. I saw them shouting
Pradeep: then go to the police station. not back to the crowd. the station
Nilesh: I'll get arrested
Pradeep: leaving is worse. and the man might still be lying there
Nilesh: ...
Pradeep: I'm calling your mama. he'll come with you
A little later Nilesh's uncle messaged Pradeep: "Found him at the tea shop. We're at the police station now. The man was taken to hospital by an auto driver. He's hurt but awake."
Nilesh: I should have stopped. I keep seeing him on the road

qa.q: Who took the injured man to hospital?
qa.a: An auto driver took him to hospital.

qa.q: Why did Nilesh ride off, and how does Nilesh feel afterwards?
qa.a: Nilesh was frightened of being beaten by the crowd, and afterwards feels guilty, unable to stop seeing the man on the road.

qa.q: What would have been a safer choice than riding off?
qa.a: Nilesh could have stopped at a safe distance, called 112 and waited for the police, so the man got help without Nilesh facing the crowd alone.

qa.q: How does Pradeep respond to Nilesh's panic?
qa.a: Pradeep is shocked but firm, pushing Nilesh toward the police station and calling his uncle to go with him.

grounding: Shows a frightened rider fleeing after hitting a pedestrian, which denies the injured man help and makes the trouble worse, until a relative steps in.
